classification.difficultyReason: Subtract two shifted absolute-value graphs, then apply the outer absolute value to the resulting signed graph.

answer.short:
$$y=\begin{cases}2,&x\le-1,\\-2x,&-1<x<0,\\2x,&0\le x<1,\\2,&x\ge1.\end{cases}$$

Join $(-1,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(1,2)$ with straight segments, extending horizontally at $y=2$ on both sides. Reflect the negative part of $|x+1|-|x-1|$ upwards.
answer.worked:
Sketch $y=|x+1|$ and $y=|x-1|$, then subtract their ordinates.

$$|x+1|-|x-1|=\begin{cases}-2,&x\le-1,\\2x,&-1<x<1,\\2,&x\ge1.\end{cases}$$

Reflect the part below the $x$-axis upwards to apply the outer absolute value.

$$y=\begin{cases}2,&x\le-1,\\-2x,&-1<x<0,\\2x,&0\le x<1,\\2,&x\ge1.\end{cases}$$

The final graph consists of the segments from $(-1,2)$ to $(0,0)$ to $(1,2)$, with horizontal rays at $y=2$.

spec.description: Horizontal rays joined by a central V; dashed negative portion shows the outer absolute-value reflection.
spec.mathematics: The final graph is y=2|x| on [-1,1] and y=2 outside that interval.
